title: Present perfect at work
goal: Hablar de experiencia y avances usando have/has + participio, since/for, already/yet.

vocabulary.example: I have already merged the PR.

exercises.prompt: I ___ in three remote companies so far.
exercises.explanation: 'So far' (hasta ahora) indica un periodo que sigue abierto → presente perfecto: 'I have worked'. El pasado simple se usa con tiempos terminados (last year, in 2020).

exercises.prompt: She has been our tech lead ___ two years.
exercises.explanation: 'For' + duración (for two years, for a month). 'Since' + punto de inicio (since 2022, since Monday).

exercises.prompt: Has the client ___ the proposal yet? (approve)
exercises.explanation: Presente perfecto = have/has + participio pasado. Para verbos regulares el participio termina en '-ed': approved.

exercises.prompt: Todavía no he terminado la tarea.
answers: I haven't finished the task yet
I have not finished the task yet
exercises.explanation: 'Todavía no' en frases negativas = 'not ... yet', y 'yet' va al FINAL de la oración.

exercises.prompt: We have ___ the documentation for the new API. (write)
exercises.explanation: Participios irregulares que debes dominar: write → written, do → done, take → taken, give → given, be → been.

exercises.answer: We have already fixed the issue
exercises.explanation: 'Already' suele ir entre 'have/has' y el participio: 'We have already fixed...'.

title: Conditionals 0, 1 and 2
goal: Expresar hechos, posibilidades reales e hipótesis.

vocabulary.example: We won't ship unless the tests pass.
My workload is heavy this week.
If we delay the launch, we lose clients.
If we had a bigger budget, we would hire more people.
If there is an outage, call the on-call engineer.

exercises.prompt: If the tests pass, we ___ the update tonight.
exercises.explanation: 1er condicional (situación real/probable): If + presente, will + verbo. 'If the tests pass, we will deploy'.

exercises.prompt: If she ___ late, we will start without her.
exercises.explanation: Error típico: poner 'will' en la parte del 'if'. Después de 'if' va PRESENTE: 'If she is late...'.

exercises.prompt: If I ___ more time, I would learn Rust. (have)
exercises.explanation: 2do condicional (hipotético/imaginario): If + pasado simple, would + verbo. 'If I had more time, I would...'.

exercises.prompt: If I ___ you, I would ask for a raise.
exercises.explanation: En el 2do condicional, lo más correcto/formal es 'were' para todas las personas: 'If I were you...'. Es una expresión fija para dar consejos.

exercises.prompt: Si el servidor falla, la aplicación se detiene.
answers: If the server fails, the application stops
If the server fails the application stops
If the server fails, the app stops
If the server fails the app stops
exercises.explanation: Condicional cero (hechos/verdades generales): If + presente, presente. Recuerda la '-s': the server fails, the app stops.

exercises.prompt: We won't meet the deadline ___ we get more help.
exercises.explanation: 'Unless' = 'if not' (a menos que). 'We won't meet the deadline unless we get help' = '...if we don't get help'.

title: Phrasal verbs & workplace idioms
title_es: Phrasal verbs y modismos de trabajo
goal: Entender los phrasal verbs y expresiones que más se usan en equipos internacionales.

vocabulary.example: I'll follow up with the client tomorrow.
Can you set up a call?
We need to figure out the root cause.
Let's make sure we're on the same page.

exercises.prompt: I'll ___ with the designer and send you an update.
exercises.explanation: 'Follow up (with someone)' = dar seguimiento. 'Give up' = rendirse; 'look up' = buscar (información).

exercises.prompt: We still need to ___ why the build is failing.
exercises.explanation: 'Figure out' = averiguar o entender algo después de pensarlo. Es muy común en el día a día técnico.

exercises.prompt: "Let's make sure we're on the same page" significa...
options: Leamos la misma página del documento
Asegurémonos de estar de acuerdo / alineados
exercises.explanation: 'Be on the same page' es un modismo: tener el mismo entendimiento sobre algo. No tiene nada que ver con páginas reales.

exercises.prompt: We ran ___ of time, so let's continue tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: 'Run out of' = quedarse sin algo (time, money, coffee). Las tres palabras van juntas.

exercises.passage:
Hi team,
Quick update: the payment integration is taking longer than expected because the provider changed their API. Maria is figuring out the new authentication flow. We'll probably push the release back to next Wednesday. I'll touch base with the client this afternoon to set expectations.
Thanks, Tom
exercises.prompt: ¿Qué va a hacer Tom esta tarde?
options: Hablar con el cliente para ajustar expectativas
exercises.explanation: 'I'll touch base with the client this afternoon to set expectations' = contactará al cliente para alinear expectativas. Quien resuelve la autenticación es María.

exercises.passage:
Hi team,
Quick update: the payment integration is taking longer than expected because the provider changed their API. Maria is figuring out the new authentication flow. We'll probably push the release back to next Wednesday. I'll touch base with the client this afternoon to set expectations.
Thanks, Tom
exercises.explanation: 'Push back' (a date/meeting/release) = posponer. Lo contrario sería 'bring forward' (adelantar).
